question: Should the remaining Android device-control, ADB-style access, and dynamic Kotlin execution work be built into the Android node, routed through a generic node/plugin tool surface, or deferred?
rationale: The remaining work changes phone authority and remote execution boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security model.

options.title: Approve narrow Android controls first
options.body: Define specific device-control commands with Android permissions, gateway allowlist behavior, docs, tests, and real-device proof before considering ADB or dynamic execution.

options.title: Wait for generic node-hosted tools
options.body: Use the generic node tool registration direction so Android does not invent a parallel dynamic tool contract.

options.title: Defer ADB and dynamic execution
options.body: Keep existing Android data/media commands and reject arbitrary phone execution until a stronger sandbox and operator-consent model exists.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow Android controls first
recommendation.body: Define specific device-control commands with Android permissions, gateway allowlist behavior, docs, tests, and real-device proof before considering ADB or dynamic execution.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior Android node command/session PRs and are the best available owner-routing signal for this security-boundary decision.
